analysis:
Examined the three changed files: DaemonStateFile.swift (new optional diagnostic fields enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery), the new SelectedModelRecovery.swift (a pure in-memory backoff/scheduler struct plus a Codable DaemonState entry type), and StartupPreloader.swift (new Summary fields failedInsufficientMemory and notAttempted, and isInsufficientMemoryLoad made internal).

Security view: no change touches the coordinator WebSocket, App Attest or serving authorization (TB-002, TB-011, T-053), key custody (A-003), or the prefix-cache crypto/TTL (T-041). The new daemon-state fields are model IDs, timestamps, counters and blocker strings, so they carry no prompt content (A-001), key material or tokens. DaemonStateFile.write is unchanged: it uses an atomic write with default permissions, and the file was already readable by local status/doctor. The new fields add only model-selection metadata, which is also publicly advertised via heartbeats. Decoding remains tolerant, since the new fields are optional and the schema stays at 1.

The recovery backoff is bounded (30s to 600s) and indexes the array with min(), so no out-of-range access. enqueue is idempotent, and the entries dictionary is keyed by model ID drawn from the selected set, so growth is bounded.

StartupPreloader changes are bookkeeping only. The memory-admission and no-evict logic is unchanged. notAttempted is slicing candidates[index...], which is in range.

The remaining integration question is that the ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery consumer (eviction of idle unselected models, with a 120s minimum idle) is not in the supplied evidence. Its eviction behavior against in-flight requests, and any effect on the advertised set or authorization, cannot be assessed from these units. I identified no regression in the supplied code.
